disease_label_per_paper: Polyarteritis nodosa with bilateral asynchronous testicular necrosis
presentation_summary: 55-year-old man with prior bilateral popliteal DVT, hypertension, and ESRD on hemodialysis developed acute left testicular pain.
Scrotal Doppler showed poor left testicular blood flow; surgery found ischemic left testicle without torsion and orchiectomy was performed.
Three weeks later he developed acute right scrotal pain and left lower-extremity pain; ultrasound showed no right testicular blood flow and right orchiectomy found a necrotic testis without torsion.

Two weeks later he developed sudden abdominal pain, a rapidly worsening livedoid abdominal patch with central impending necrosis, penile pain/swelling/dusky cold glans, and transient left-eye vision loss.
Skin biopsy showed thrombotic vasculopathy with leukocytoclastic vasculitis, and he was diagnosed with PAN by clinical criteria and histopathology.

risk_context.source_text_value: ESRD secondary to focal segmental glomerulonephritis on hemodialysis
Bilateral popliteal DVT six months before presentation
Hepatitis B surface and core antibodies within normal limits

observations.source_text_value: Acute onset left testicular pain during hemodialysis
Scrotal Doppler showed poor left testicular blood flow; surgery found ischemic testis
Left shoulder pain radiating down the left upper extremity
Three weeks later acute right-sided scrotal pain
Right scrotal ultrasound showed no blood flow; exploration found necrotic testis without torsion
Sudden abdominal pain before abdominal skin changes
Abdominal skin patch 19 x 14 cm with central impending necrosis 9 x 12 cm
Penile pain, swelling, dusky cold glans, and loss of glans sensation
Temporary left-eye vision loss resolving after one hour
CRP described as within normal limits
observations.quality_note: No numeric CRP value was reported; value encodes normal qualitative state rather than mg/L.

observations.source_text_value: ESR described as within normal limits
observations.quality_note: No numeric ESR value was reported; value encodes normal qualitative state rather than mm/hr.

observations.source_text_value: Hepatitis B surface/core antibodies within normal limits

imaging.source_text_value: Poor left testicular flow; later no right testicular flow
Anterior abdominal wall skin thickening, subcutaneous edema, and fat stranding without distinct hematoma
Pulsatile penile artery flow and normal penile-brachial index despite ischemic exam

microbiology.source_text_value: Hepatitis B surface/core antibodies within normal limits
Hepatitis C virus antibodies within normal limits

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Anterior abdominal wall biopsy showed thrombotic vasculopathy with leukocytoclastic vasculitis
PAN criteria met: mononeuropathy, testicular pain, biopsy with granulocytes, livedo reticularis

actual_treatment: enoxaparin, warfarin, and aspirin after right orchiectomy
cyclophosphamide, later stopped for wound infection

outcome.clinical_course: No further ischemic events at 6-month follow-up after steroids/cyclophosphamide, though cyclophosphamide was stopped because of wound infection.
outcome.source_text_value: No further ischemic events at 6-month follow-up

quality_warnings: Testicular ultrasound and ischemic operative findings are ordinary ischemic manifestations, while biopsy evidence is confirmatory.
Normal ESR/CRP were reported without numeric values; qualitative normal observations are flagged by unit and quality_note.
